Commentary.Commentary: Tamim Iqbal then goes up to collect the series win trophy and joins his teammates for the celebration as well. That is it then from this game and from the ODI series as well between Bangladesh and Ireland with the hosts winning the three-game series 2-0. The action now moves to the three-game T20I series and the first game will be played on Monday, the 27th of March at the Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium in Chattogram. That game will begin at 1.30 pm IST (8 am GMT) but you can join us a lot earlier for the build-up. Cheers!

Tamim Iqbal says that the way they played the whole series was unbelievable and stringing two solid batting performance back-to-back and now in this game, the pacers did a brilliant job as well. Adds that players like Mehidy Hasan when he starts performing with the bat, it helps a lot and that is the way forward as their bowling unit is pretty settled. Mentions that winning by 10 wickets is special and the way they chased down the runs shows authority and applauds Litton Das for his brilliant innings as well. Ends by saying that a lot of credit goes to the coach who encourages them to play on such sporting wickets.

Mushfiqur Rahim is the PLAYER OF THE SERIES. He says that they had another series win and all the boys chipped in really well. On his batting in this series, he says that the conditions were good for batting and the top order had set it up nicely for him to go big. Mentions that he is happy to chip in with both the bat and with the gloves as well.

Hasan Mahmud is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his brilliant bowling display. Starts by saying that he is very grateful and is very excited for his first-ever five-wicket haul. Adds that the wicket and the weather both were good for pace bowling and he enjoyed it out there. On Alan Donald, he says that he has worked really hard with the bowlers and it can be seen.

Andy Balbirnie, the captain of Ireland says that they are very disappointed an the last few days reflect how poor they have been but he can't fault the efforts of the guys. Mentions that naturally you expect the spinners to play a big part here but the opposition pacers have been brilliant and they didn't adapt well. Adds that they had a pretty good T20 World Cup in Australia and they know they can do well in that format and are looking forward to rising up to the challenge.
The Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Andy Balbirnie won the toss and opted to bat first in conditions that definitely had something in it for the fast bowlers. This decision seemed to be influenced by the fact that they conceded in excess of 300 twice in the games before but it turned out to be a disastrous one. Hasan Mahmud was simply brilliant at the start, getting the ball to move in the air and off the deck as well and he ripped through the top order of Ireland. Taskin Ahmed too supported him well, striking from the other end. After the first 10 overs, Curtis Campher and Lorcan Tucker put up a decent partnership of 42 runs before the latter was dismissed by Ebadot Hossain. This led to another collapse as Hasan Mahmud came back to end with a five-wicket haul and Ireland somehow managed to cross the 100-run mark. Coming to the chase, it only went one way as the openers of Bangladesh didn't waste much timed and sealed a first-ever 10-wicket victory for them in ODIs.

There is nothing much to talk about the Irish bowling and truth be told, they never had a chance of defending this meager total. However, both Mark Adair and Graham Hume were guilty of bowling some really loose deliveries at the start of the chase. Young spinner Matthew Humphreys then bowled a really tidy first over only to concede five wides on the last ball and extra delivery was hit away for a maximum as well. Curtis Campher did bowl in good channels but he too was put away for boundaries. All in all, a day to forget for the Irish side and they will look to bounce back after this.

With just 102 runs to win, Bangladesh also seemed in the driving seat but the way in which the openers attacked was something special. The pair hammered the Irish pacers to all parts of the ground early in the first Powerplay and took full advantage of the fielding restrictions. Tamim Iqbal was the aggressor at first but then Litton Das matched him shot for shot, even going one better and notching up a half-ton and remaining unbeaten on 50 off just 38 balls. Tamim Iqbal too remained unbeaten on a-run-a-ball 41 and hit the winning runs for his side.

What a flex this has been from Bangladesh and not just in this game but throughout this ODI series. In the first game, they won by their biggest margin of runs ever and now they have achieved a victory by 10 wickets for the first time as well in ODIs. Ireland on the other hand have simply been cast aside here and they will now look to forget this series before the start of the T20Is.
There it is, Bangladesh have done it! Back of a length outside off, Tamim Iqbal stays back and just guides it behind backward point for a single. Bangladesh win by 10 wickets!
On a length and around off, eased away toward extra cover.

FOUR! FIFTY for Litton Das and he has made it look really out there. Floated up full and on leg stump, a slight shuffle from Litton and he sweeps it along the turf into the square leg fence. Scores are now level!
FOUR! Too short and wide, Litton Das hangs back and slaps it away wide of the diving man at backward point for a boundary.
Short and wide outside off, Litton Das has to reach for it and he cuts it hard but straight to cover-point.
Shortens the length and bowls it around middle, Litton Das backs away and pushes it toward mid off.
Nicely drifted onto middle, Litton Das leans forward to defend.
Pitched up around off, pushed out toward point.
This is banged in short and Litton Das comes forward forcing the pull in front of mid-wicket for a single.
Back of a length outside off, dabbed down toward backward point.
Length ball, angling into middle, Litton Das looks to flick but gets a leading edge onto the off side.
FOUR! Pitched up outside off. Litton Das leans on and just pushes it off the middle of the bat through the cover region for a boundary.
Good length in that channel around off and seaming away nicely. Litton Das looks to play on the up but is beaten past the outside edge.
Flatter delivery around off, cut away to cover-point.
Tamim Iqbal gives the charge and Matthew Humphreys shortens the length. Tamim adjusts and keeps it out.
SIX! Tossed up around off stump, Tamim Iqbal skips down the pitch and lofts it straight back over the bowler's head for a maximum.
Excellent stop! Floated up around off, Tamim Iqbal gets into position early and nails the reverse sweep. Curtis Campher at short fine leg dives to his right and stops a certain boundary.
Full and on the pads, this is flicked away over mid-wicket for a single.
On a length and drifted into the pads, Litton Das defends it out.
Powerplay 2! Ireland can now have a maximum of 4 players outside the inner circle.
Maiden! Fuller and on off and middle, Tamim Iqbal just defends it out. After the end of the first Powerplay, Bangladesh are 81/0! They now need just 21 more runs for the win.
Length ball around leg stump and slanting back in, Tamim Iqbal looks to lean forward and flick but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Very full on off stump, Tamim Iqbal drives it toward mid on.
Length ball around middle and leg, nudged away toward mid-wicket.
On a good length, close to the off stump, Tamim Iqbal punches it off the back foot toward cover-point.
Full and around leg stump, flicked away straight to square leg.
Floated full and round middle, Tamim Iqbal nudges it past the man at square leg and picks up a run.
Drifted into the legs, Litton Das shuffles past the leg stump and knocks it through mid off for a single.
Quicker one around off, cut away hard but straight to backward point.
FOUR! Two in a row! Dragged down on middle, Litton Das uses the depth of the crease and jabs it over the infield and the ball goes into the cow corner fence.
FOUR! Pierces the gap! Shorter and outside off, Litton Das backs away and cuts it in between backward point and point for a boundary.
Flatter delivery around off, eased away toward point.
Full and on off stump, punched away on the up to mid on.
WIDE! Length ball, spilled down the leg side, Lorcan Tucker does well to dive to his right and save the boundary. Wide called.
Full and outside off, driving off the outer half of the bat toward deep backward point for one.
FOUR! It's just too easy at the moment! Shorter and outside off, Litton Das slaps this one over the cover region and the ball goes into the boundary.

Good effort in the field! Short of a length around off, Litton Das stands tall and short-arm jabs it through wide mid on. Graham Hume sprints after it and manages to pull it back in, saves two runs for his side.
Full and around ooff, Litton Das looks to drive straight but toe ends it to the right of mid off for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Sweetly timed! Length ball outside off, Litton Das puts his front foot forward and punches it on the up through the cover region for a boundary.
WIDE! Starts off with a full and wide one, swinging further away. Wide called.

SIX! Adding insult to injury as the extra delivery goes the distance! This is floated up around leg stump, Tamim Iqbal gets down on one knee and slog-sweeps it firmly over the square leg fence for a maximum.

FIVE WIDES! A really tidy over is ruined by this delivery and the 50 comes up for Bangladesh now. This is tossed up around leg stump and turning down leg sharply. The ball beats the bat and eludes the keeper before running away into the fence.
Full again on the pads, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
Thei is fired in full and on off stump, Tamim Iqbal jams it back to the bowler.
Slows it up a bit and floats it on off and middle, Tamim Iqbal shapes up for the sweep but defends it instead.
Quicker one around middle, Tamim Iqbal defends it out.
Starts off with a fuller one around off, Tamim Iqbal looks to gets inside the lien and paddle it away but misses. The ball goes off the pads toward short leg.
Matthew Humphreys comes into the attack now.
On a fuller length and angling into the pads, this is flicked away down to fine leg for a single.
Short of a good length on off, Tamim Iqbal goes back in his crease to make the block.
Good length on the stumps, nudged leg side by Tamim Iqbal.

Top effort! Good length outside off, Litton Das slashes it on the up behind the man at backward point. Harry Tector there flies to his left and gets his right hand on it but fails to hold on to a tough chance. They get a single.
On a good length around off, seaming away, Litton Das blocks it out on the off side.
FOUR! Poor delivery and put away. Short and wide with no real pace behind it. Litton Das taps it away in front of point and picks up a boundary.
This is pitched up in that channel outside off and swinging away, left alone by Tamim Iqbal.
Comes from around the stumps now and bowls it on a good length around off. The ball nips back in sharply and Tamim Iqbal almost gets chopped on.
FOUR! Up and over! Length ball outside off, enough width on offer for Tamim Iqbal to free his arms and slap it over cover-point for a boundary.
Fullish delivery on the pads, Litton Das pushes this one away in front of the man at deep square leg for a single.

Good cricket all-around! Pitched up on off and middle, Tamim Iqbal plays a lovely straight drive through mid on. Andy McBrine there does well to chase it down and keep it in play. Three runs are taken.
Keeps the length full and brings it close to the off stump, Tamim Iqbal gets on the front foot to defend.
WIDE! And again! A touch fuller and spilled beyond the tramline outside off. Wide called.
WIDE! On a length, well outside off and swinging further away. Left alone for a wide.
Good length around off, pushed out toward cover.
Fuller and on the leg pole, Tamim Iqbal leans on and nudges it 'round the corner for a single.
Leg bye! Good length on the pads, Litton Das misses the flick and the ball goes off the pads onto the leg side. They get a leg bye.
Fullish length on the fifth stump line and swinging away, Litton Das leaves it alone.
Back of a length and around off, Litton Das hops back and gets behind the line to defend it out.
On a good length, pushed well outside the off stump, Litton Das let's it through to the keeper.
FOUR! This is bowled shorter and around leg stump, Tamim Iqbal whips it away off his hips and finds the fence at square leg.

Good length around off, Tamim Iqbal blocks it to the right of the bowler and looks for a run. Mark Adair picks up the ball and fires in a throw at the stumps. Tamim turns back and dives back in but gets hit on the body.
WIDE! Fullish delivery, slanted well across the left-hander and goes beyond the tramline outside off. Wide called.
FOUR! Cracking shot! Overpitched outside off, Tamim Iqbal lays into the shot and stylishly hammers it away through extra cover for another boundary. Tamim even holds the pose this time around.
Fraction shorter over leg stump and jagging back in. Tamim Iqbal gets cramped for room and gets a blow on the thigh pad.
FOUR! This is pitched up around off, angling away, Tamim Iqbal gets on the front foot and drives it gloriously through extra cover for a boundary.

Very full down leg and swinging further away. Tamim Iqbal looks to flick but misses and the Irish players appeal as the keeper, Lorcan Tucker collects the ball. No wide given by the umpire and Andy Balbirnie reviews it. The UltraEdge though confirms that the ball missed the bat and just flicked the pad. A review is wasted but at this point it was worth a go.
FOUR! Eased away! Short ball offering a lot of width outside the off stump. Litton Das just hangs back and taps it wide of the point fielder for a boundary.
Pitches it up outside off and swinging away, Litton Das doesn't play at it.
FOUR! Litton Das has seen enough and decides to be aggressive. Back of a length outside off, Litton Das fetches and pulls this one well over wide mid on and the ball trickles away into the fence.
Perfect length in that channel around off, Litton Das watchfully blocks this one off the front foot.
Good length around the top of off, this is nudged down in front of cover.
Hits the deck hard and bowls it around off, Litton Das stands outside the crease and plays it down toward backward point.
Graham Hume to bowl from the opposite end.
On a good length and angled well across the left-hander, Tamim Iqbal leaves it alone. So, 6 runs off the first over, a breezy start here for Bangladesh.
Length ball around leg stump, this is nudged away to square leg.
Pitches this one up on leg stump, shaping it back in. Tamim Iqbal falls over as he flicks this one down to fine leg for a couple of runs.
Fullish length outside off and swinging away, left alone for the keeper to collect.
FOUR! Up and over! This is short and wide, Tamim Iqbal throws his hands at it and slaps it over the point region for a boundary. Tamim Iqbal and Bangladesh are underway!
Starts off with a good-length delivery around off and angling away. Tamim Iqbal has a feel for it but is beaten past the outside edge.
